mainTopic: Selling a field 'with its markers and borders' (בסימניו ובמצריו): when the measurement is off by exactly one sixth (שתות), does the sale stand, or must the seller pay back the difference?
overview: The משנה teaches that when a field is sold 'with its markers and borders' (בסימניו ובמצריו), a measuring error of less than a sixth (שתות) does not matter. A bigger error means the seller must deduct from the price. The גמרא brings a מחלוקת about an error of exactly one sixth. רב הונא says exactly a sixth is like a small error, so the sale stands. רב יהודה says it is like a big error, so the seller deducts. Each one reads the words of the משנה to fit his view. The גמרא then challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא that compares this sale to שום הדיינין, the judges' appraisal, where exactly a sixth counts as a big error. רב הונא answers that the comparison is only partial: the two cases share the measure of a sixth, but the judges' sale is cancelled while here the buyer keeps the field. The גמרא then begins a story about רב פפא buying land from a certain man, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: selling a field with its markers and borders
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a field sold with its borders is off by less than a sixth, the buyer keeps it as is. If the error is bigger, up to a sixth, the seller deducts.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sells a field 'with its markers and borders': if the size is off by less than a sixth, the field belongs to the buyer as is. 'Until a sixth', the seller must deduct.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rule for a field sold with clearly marked borders when the actual size turns out a bit different from what was stated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the seller pointed out the exact borders, the stated size is less central, so small errors are forgiven. An error under a sixth is ignored ('הגיעו'). A bigger error means the seller must 'ינכה', deduct money. The words 'עד שתות' are unclear about what happens at exactly one sixth, and that is what the גמרא will argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
Markers or signs that identify the field
Borders or boundaries of the field
One sixth
Literally 'it has reached him': the sale stands and the buyer keeps it as is
He deducts: the seller gives back part of the price

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he sold a field 'with its markers and its borders':
less than a sixth, it is his;
until a sixth, he deducts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the משנה of this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a sale 'with markers and borders', an error of less than a sixth is ignored. A larger error requires the seller to deduct from the price.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב יהודה disagree about exactly a sixth
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says an error of exactly a sixth is like less than a sixth. רב יהודה says it is like more than a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב הונא said a sixth is like less than a sixth. רב יהודה said a sixth is like more than a sixth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת between two אמוראים about the exact borderline case: an error of exactly one sixth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, exactly a sixth is still a forgiven error, so the sale stands. For רב יהודה, exactly a sixth already counts as a big error, so the seller must deduct. The whole argument is about which side of the line the number one sixth itself falls on.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה
Less than a sixth
More than a sixth

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree about less than a sixth and more than a sixth. The argument is only about an error of EXACTLY one sixth.

phrases.english: Gemara:
It was stated: Rav Huna said:
A sixth is like less than a sixth.
Rav Yehuda said:
A sixth is like more than a sixth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a מחלוקת about the unclear borderline in the משנה's words 'עד שתות'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: exactly a sixth means the sale stands. רב יהודה: exactly a sixth means the seller deducts.

steps.title: How רב הונא reads the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads the משנה as: less than a sixth, including exactly a sixth, the sale stands. More than a sixth, the seller deducts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, who says a sixth is like less than a sixth, explains that the משנה means this: less than a sixth, with a sixth included, it is his. More than a sixth, he deducts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב הונא fits his view into the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא puts exactly a sixth into the first clause, together with 'פחות משתות'. So the second clause, 'עד שתות', must really mean an error that goes beyond a sixth.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: introduces a reading of the source
Included

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: שְׁתוּת כְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁתוּת –
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: a sixth is like less than a sixth;
this is what it is saying:
less than a sixth, with a sixth included, it is his.
More than a sixth, he deducts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רב הונא's view from step 2 fits the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Exactly a sixth belongs with the 'הגיעו' clause, so only more than a sixth requires a deduction.

steps.title: How רב יהודה reads the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads the משנה as: less than a sixth, the sale stands. Up to a sixth, including exactly a sixth, the seller deducts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, who says a sixth is like more than a sixth, explains that the משנה means this: less than a sixth, it is his. Until a sixth, with a sixth included, he deducts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רב יהודה fits his view into the same words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה reads the משנה at face value: only 'less than a sixth' is forgiven. Exactly a sixth falls into the 'ינכה' clause, so the seller must deduct.

keyTerms.meaning: Until a sixth: here read as including exactly a sixth

steps.whatToRemember: Same words, two readings. רב הונא puts exactly a sixth with 'הגיעו' (the sale stands). רב יהודה puts it with 'ינכה' (the seller deducts).

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: שְׁתוּת כְּיוֹתֵר מִשְּׁתוּת –
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: a sixth is like more than a sixth;
this is what it is saying:
less than a sixth, it is his.
Until a sixth, with a sixth included, he deducts.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: שְׁתוּת כְּיוֹתֵר מִשְּׁתוּת – הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching reading for the other side, רב יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Exactly a sixth belongs with the 'ינכה' clause, so the seller must deduct.

steps.title: A ברייתא compares this sale to the judges' appraisal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: in a sale 'with markers and borders', if the field is a sixth less or a sixth more, it is like שום הדיינין and the buyer keeps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: 'With its markers and borders': if he gave a sixth less or a sixth more, it is like the judges' appraisal, and it is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the source. The point of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares a sale with marked borders to שום הדיינין, a sale of property done by a court's appraisal. That comparison is what the גמרא will use to attack רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave less
He gave more
The judges' appraisal: a sale of property carried out by the court's valuation

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'With its markers and its borders':
if he gave a sixth less or gave a sixth more,
it is like the judges' appraisal,
it is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to test the מחלוקת, aimed at רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that exactly a sixth is like less than a sixth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא compares this sale to שום הדיינין. The next step spells out why that comparison causes a problem.

steps.title: With the judges' appraisal, a sixth counts as more than a sixth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that with שום הדיינין, an error of exactly a sixth is treated like more than a sixth. That seems to go against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with the judges' appraisal, a sixth is treated like more than a sixth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the actual challenge against רב הונא, based on the ברייתא's comparison to שום הדיינין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a court appraisal, an error of exactly a sixth already counts as a big error. Since the ברייתא says our case is 'like שום הדיינין', it suggests that here too exactly a sixth should count as big. That fits רב יהודה and contradicts רב הונא. The next step gives רב הונא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely: introduces a known fact used to press the challenge

steps.whyThisMatters: The challenge borrows a known rule from another area of law (court appraisals) to decide our borderline case. This shows how a comparison in a ברייתא can carry over a whole set of rules.

phrases.english: But the judges' appraisal,
is a case where a sixth is like more than a sixth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up by the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא: exactly a sixth is like less than a sixth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא likens this sale to שום הדיינין, where exactly a sixth is like more than a sixth. So here too exactly a sixth should count as more, which goes against רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא: The comparison to the judges' assessment is only partial
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the ברייתא cannot mean a full comparison to שום הדיינין, since it says הגיעו while with שום הדיינין the sale is cancelled. The comparison is only about the measure of a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא could answer you: Even by your own reasoning, there is a problem, because the ברייתא says 'it is his' (the sale stands)! So the ברייתא must mean: it is like the judges' assessment, and also not like the judges' assessment. It is like the judges' assessment in the measure of a sixth. It is not like the judges' assessment, because there the sale is cancelled, while here the buyer keeps it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רב הונא from step 6. It shows that the ברייתא's comparison to שום הדיינין cannot be a full comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the ברייתא copies every detail of שום הדיינין, including how it treats exactly a sixth. But the ברייתא itself says הגיעו, while with שום הדיינין an error of that size cancels the sale, so even the challenger must admit the comparison is not complete. Once the comparison covers only the measure of a sixth, the ברייתא no longer proves anything against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning: turning the question back on the one asking
Whereas there: sets up a contrast with the other case
The sale is cancelled

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא compares the case to שום הדיינין only in the measure of a sixth, not in the result. With שום הדיינין the sale is cancelled. In a sale 'with markers and borders', the buyer keeps the field. So the challenge to רב הונא falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Like the judges' assessment and not like the judges' assessment' is not a contradiction. It means the two cases are alike in one detail (the sixth) and different in another (the result).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move. When a source compares two cases, we cannot assume the comparison covers every detail, especially when the source itself shows a difference.

phrases.english: Rav Huna could say to you:
And by your reasoning, it teaches 'it is his'!
phrases.notes: He means: the ברייתא says the buyer keeps the field, and that does not fit שום הדיינין either.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּשׁוּם הַדַּיָּינִין – וְלֹא כְּשׁוּם הַדַּיָּינִין;
phrases.english: Rather, it is like the judges' assessment, and not like the judges' assessment;
Like the judges' assessment in the measure of a sixth,
And not like the judges' assessment,
For there, the sale is cancelled;
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of a judges' assessment.

phrases.english: Whereas here, it is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב הונא raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison: the ברייתא compares to שום הדיינין only in the measure of a sixth.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's mention of שום הדיינין means the case follows every rule of the judges' assessment, including how exactly a sixth is treated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is only about the measure of a sixth. The result differs: the judges' sale is cancelled, while here the buyer keeps the field. So the ברייתא is no challenge to רב הונא.

steps.title: A story begins: רב פפא buys land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new story: רב פפא bought land from a certain man.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא bought land from a certain man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new story. It only gives the opening facts here, and the rest of the story comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After רב הונא's answer to the challenge, the גמרא moves to a real case about buying land. This line only introduces who bought and what was bought, so the halachic question has not appeared yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Bought
Land, a field
A certain man (the גמרא does not give his name)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa bought land
From a certain man,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא זְבַן אַרְעָא מֵהַהוּא גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story after רב הונא's answer to the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line sets up the facts of רב פפא's purchase of land.
